purpose: Four-state census of every instrument this EP emits. The `uninvoked` and `ambiguous` arrays are MACHINE-GENERATED by audit_instruments.py --write-baseline and are drift-checked by --check. Everything under `hand` is hand-classified: `unreachable`, `misnamed` and `absent` are not decidable from text.
consumers: Trinity: M0 criterion 12 wiring census. Consume this file rather than building a second one.

states.uninvoked: exists, never called from production code (tests do not count)
states.unreachable: called, but its output goes somewhere nothing reads
states.misnamed: wired, invoked, correct — and its name misdescribes its content
states.out-of-frame: wired, invoked, read, arithmetically correct - and the event it counts CANNOT OCCUR in the frame it observes, so its zero is not a measurement. Reports UNOBSERVABLE, never 0 (DESIGN.md 10.0.1 R12). A FIFTH state, not a split of `unreachable`: unreachable is fixed by wiring a reader, out-of-frame is fixed only by changing the world being measured (here, 6.5's one-VkDevice rule). Different repairs, so they must not share a name.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: trace summary line `compute: first-record=N replay=N rerecord=N`; now prints `record-path breakdown NOT WIRED` when all three are zero
uninvoked_notes.excludes: everything. Zero production callers. It is the ONLY instrument that could falsify Phase::Record's former caveat that recording is 'amortised across replays'; that caveat shipped in every ph:"X" span for weeks and was false.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: FLAGGED — wiring it requires a vk/session.rs edit (Switch's file). Artifact now says NOT WIRED instead of printing zeros.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: log_slowest_ops() table, now wired from ep.rs Drop and printing `per-op host time NOT WIRED` on an empty map
uninvoked_notes.excludes: all per-op host attribution. The producer has no caller, so the table was empty; before this session the reporter ALSO returned silently, so the absence had two layers and printed nothing at all.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: PARTIAL FIX — reporter wired + NOT WIRED message. Producer wiring belongs to op translation.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: alloc_device_buffer_binds in the counters JSON (added this session; reads 0)
uninvoked_notes.excludes: the 95% transfer ceiling. Zero production callers is the structural reason alloc_device_authoritative_spans is 0: nothing has ever bound one of our device buffers.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: FLAGGED (feature, not defect) — the bind seam is Switch's persistent-residency work. Counter wired ahead of it deliberately.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: alloc_device_authoritative_spans + alloc_device_authoritative_ceiling + the audit sentence in every staging_verdict branch
uninvoked_notes.excludes: nothing yet — it is the single documented increment point for the counter that will be quoted when residency lands. Uninvoked BY DESIGN until then.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: INTENTIONAL — audited by ceiling (device_backed - staged) and by bind traffic so it cannot be over-claimed.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: none in production; to_json_with_equiv is the wired path (counters.rs:355)
uninvoked_notes.excludes: the equivalence verdict — it hardcodes UNMEASURED. This is the residue of Defect C (two writers, one artifact) and is now the only remaining caller-less half.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: FLAGGED — harmless while unused; delete or fold if it stays uninvoked.

uninvoked_notes.artifact: none yet, by construction - and that is the point. The observable proxy is alloc_device_frame in the counters JSON, which reads SPLIT-DEVICE on every run until this function acquires a caller and SHARED afterwards. That key is the artifact whose content varies with this function's input (R10).
uninvoked_notes.excludes: n/a - it is the 6.5 seam, not a measurement. Listed so its wiring status is machine-checked rather than asserted.
uninvoked_notes.disposition: FLAGGED for Switch, who owns the seam (6.5: the side that owns the lifetime owns the seam). vk/host_device_memory.rs added to INSTRUMENT_FILES so the baseline goes red the day it is called and somebody must look at the frame.

unreachable.instrument: allocator.rs GetStats KVPs (Limit, InUse, NumAllocs, MaxInUse, NumFrees, LiveSpans, QuarantinedSpans, QuarantineRetired, FailedLookups)
unreachable.artifact: NONE. Nothing in this repository calls ORT's GetStats, so no run has ever produced these nine numbers.
unreachable.excludes: everything they measure. failed_lookups is the costly one: its own doc says 'non-zero always indicates a bug somewhere', and it was only observable through an API nothing calls. Same shape as quarantine_retired, which we asserted had never fired while nothing had ever written it down.
unreachable.disposition: FIXED for failed_lookups — plumbed process-wide (tally::on_failed_lookup at all three increment sites) and emitted as alloc_failed_lookups in the counters JSON, which the harness DOES read. The other eight remain unreachable and are partly duplicated by process-wide keys.

unreachable.artifact: the append-only claim log — but record_audit (registry.rs:1639) is the wired writer and record writes a THINNER line to the SAME file
unreachable.excludes: the audit fields. Two writers, one artifact, different schemas: the exact shape of counters Defect C, where a run ending in a dispatch silently lost 27 keys. It has not bitten because record has no caller.
unreachable.disposition: FLAGGED — Mouse's file, do not fix. Screen reports it as AMBIGUOUS, not uninvoked, because logging.rs has a parameter named `record`.

misnamed.artifact: every ph:"X" span in the GPU trace JSON, plus the host-time table in the tracer summary
misnamed.excludes: nothing — it INCLUDES what nobody expected. It brackets vkBeginCommandBuffer..vkEndCommandBuffer, and the staging memcpy runs inside it while record_transfer deliberately emits no ph:"X" span. 96% of `record` is upload. Any aggregation over ph:"X" spans structurally cannot see upload as a separate term, so '68% recording, transfers bounded by the 30.4% fence-wait' was wrong in both halves.
misnamed.disposition: FIXED in the artifact, not by rename (compatibility outranks elegance): caveat() rewritten to say it CONTAINS upload/readback and cite the 96%; a machine-readable `nested_in` arg is now emitted on every span; the summary table indents children, derives the sibling set from Phase::nested_in(), and prints a SIBLING TOTAL so nobody sums the column by hand.

misnamed.excludes: vk::session's ~1997.6 MiB-per-inference host staging. It verifies ALLOCATOR SPANS only. Its own help text said 'fail unless nothing was host-staged', which is the misnaming.
misnamed.disposition: FIXED — help text corrected and the PASS path now prints an explicit exclusion note naming the staging it is blind to. Exit-code semantics unchanged (it already fails the MIRRORED state).

absent.artifact: none — record_transfer feeds totals only, and emits no ph:"X" span by design
absent.excludes: any timeline view of upload. The 96% figure is derivable only from the summary totals, not from the trace JSON.
absent.disposition: FLAGGED — emitting a nested span is a vk/session.rs change (Switch).

out_of_frame.artifact: the counters JSON, and the authoritative-audit sentence in every staging_verdict() branch
out_of_frame.excludes: everything, in the SPLIT-DEVICE and OFF frames. The counter can only move when the engine binds one of the provider's buffers, and while the provider holds its own VkDevice (6.5) no dispatch on the session's device can bind them at all. The zero was being read as 'residency has not landed yet'; it actually meant 'this question has no answer in this run'.
out_of_frame.disposition: FIXED. The artifact emits the JSON string "UNOBSERVABLE" instead of the number 0 whenever alloc_device_frame != SHARED, so a reader doing arithmetic on it fails loudly. New keys alloc_device_frame / alloc_device_frame_device carry frame provenance; epctl prints the frame on the --require-device-memory PASS path. Falsifiers: counters::a_pinned_authoritative_counter_reports_unobservable_and_never_zero, allocator::a_zero_authoritative_count_in_a_foreign_frame_says_unobservable_not_unwired, allocator::a_nonzero_authoritative_count_in_a_split_frame_is_not_credible.

out_of_frame.excludes: vk::session's staging copies, ALL of them. It counts only copies made by the allocator's own provider, on the provider's own VkDevice, and only with ONNXRUNTIME_EP_VULKAN_DEVICE_MEMORY=1. It read 0 on a run whose cmd_upload phase was 15.2 s. Both numbers correct; different worlds - R12's specimen.
out_of_frame.disposition: NOT renamed: it is correct in its own frame, and compatibility outranks elegance. Tagged instead, by alloc_device_frame. The session-side accounting is the separate, unconditional session_staging_upload_bytes. The two must NEVER be added.

ledger.quarantine: UNOBSERVED, not clean: peak depth 423 against a window of 4096, retired 0, use_after_free 0. The detector was NOT exhausted (peak is 10% of the window), so use_after_free == 0 is a genuine negative for this pattern — 'we checked', not 'we could not have seen it'. Distinct from quarantine_retired, which was 'we could not have seen it' until it was plumbed off the GetStats path.
ledger.alloc_device_authoritative_spans: UNOBSERVABLE, not 0, as of 6.5's ruling: structurally pinned while the memory provider holds a second VkDevice, and R12 forbids any criterion naming a pinned instrument - so M1's weight-residency criterion is read against device_upload_bytes on the session's device instead. It passes through THREE distinct states and each gets its own sentence: UNOBSERVABLE (no frame in which a result could exist) -> UNWIRED zero (frame SHARED, but allocator::tally::on_device_authoritative still has no production caller) -> a measurement (transfer::device_buffer_for called). The word 'zero' never appears alone.

states_ordering: absent -> uninvoked -> unreachable -> out-of-frame -> misnamed, by how late the failure is discoverable. R10 catches the first two. Nothing but a second, independent instrument catches the last two.
